note: Negative control for answer-key-6.2.4.json: fast-jwt 6.3.1 fixes all three advisories scored there. `seeded` is empty; `decoys` are the fixed code at 6.3.1 lines (verified against the extracted tree with `node benchmark/real/fetch.mjs npm/fast-jwt 6.3.1 --check --dest <run>`), so `decoy false positives` counts verified findings that still report a fixed advisory. A verified finding that matches nothing is listed for review (README, findings outside the key). Same format and matching rules as benchmark/answer-key.json. By design, a caller that explicitly allows only HS algorithms still has its key used as a raw secret (detection is skipped); that is documented behaviour, not a decoy.

decoys.why: The decoder rejects array payloads (Array.isArray), so claim validators always see an object.
A key without a PEM header that parses as an asymmetric JWK, a JWKS or an array of JWKs is refused before the raw-secret fallback.
createVerifier() requires a usable key unless 'none' is the only allowed algorithm, and refuses a key when it is.
